summary: Restored monitoring-only access to the private artifact-cache v2 endpoint and node-exporter while preserving the cache-port allowlist for approved build/runtime consumers.

verification.check: PVE VM firewall compile and service
verification.observed: The VM 180 policy was rendered from vm.fw.j2, the existing file was backed up, the policy compiled, pve-firewall restarted, and the service reports enabled/running.
From the monitoring VM, Blackbox Exporter using http_2xx_follow_redirects returned probe_http_status_code 200 and probe_success 1 for the private registry v2 endpoint.
From the monitoring VM, the artifact-cache /metrics endpoint on TCP/9100 returned HTTP 200.
The monitoring VM can reach TCP/5001 and TCP/9100; TCP/5002, TCP/5003, and TCP/5004 remain blocked.
Both docker-build and docker-runtime can reach artifact-cache TCP ports 5001 through 5004.
All four cache containers are running in host network mode, the Docker bridge has zero attached containers, and the local registry v2 endpoint returns HTTP 200.

notes: Only the artifact-cache VM firewall file and the artifact-cache guest nftables policy were applied; the whole Proxmox network role was intentionally not run because the current identity overlay fails its self-referential uplink safety guard.
The prior VM firewall file is retained on the Proxmox host at /root/.lv3-vm-180.fw.backup-20261012T1744Z; its SHA-256 was cc41aa2a2a9b3b471ad325d8e783d106698d42edf11daaeec7ae92b69488908f.
